subject: Post-demo: Clarify SLO parity + next reliability probes
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.inference>
To: Asha Patel <asha@heliocare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Clarify SLO parity + next reliability probes

Hi Asha — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the bakeoff you asked for.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goals: 99.9% availability, <100ms p50 generation for short prompts, predictable cost under sustained 1k rps.
- Concern areas: rate limiting behavior under large concurrency, failover during AZ/region loss, cold-start/kv-cache warmup impact.

Proposed immediate artifacts we can deliver this week:
1) SLO parity matrix (Redwood vs Hyperscaler X vs Hyperscaler Y) — includes uptime, rate-limit semantics, burst behavior, documented error codes.
2) A short synthetic test harness and test config we can hand to your infra team to run in your staging environment (we'll provide a k8s job + script).
3) Logs & demo traces from today's run attached (heliocare-slo-comparison.xlsx + rdwd-demo-logs.tar.gz).

Ask from you:
- Confirm the two most critical failure modes you want exercised (e.g., single-AZ outage, token-throttling at 4k rps, node preemption).
- Share any internal SLA wording we should align on (example: rolling restart window tolerance).

Next steps timeline:
- EOD Mon: deliver SLO parity matrix and test harness + recommended probe definitions.
- Wed: quick sync to align probe scheduling and access for staging.
- Following week: coordinated run (we'll assist and observe).

If that sounds right I can drop the matrix and test configs into the Drive link and open a HubSpot task for scheduling.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0139

Attachments: heliocare-slo-comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet), rdwd-demo-logs.tar.gz (logs)
From: Asha Patel <asha@heliocare.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops@heliocare.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarify SLO parity + next reliability probes

Thanks Mina — this is very helpful. Two quick clarifications from our side:  

1) Failure modes: top priority is single-AZ outage (we've seen noisy neighbor crashes before) and sudden token throttling when traffic bursts from our mobile app (usually ~3–5s bursts up to 3k rps). Cold-start is lower priority but still good to understand.
2) SLA language: our procurement team needs clear definitions for what counts as an availability incident (we can share our template by EOD).

We'd like the SLO parity matrix to show both observed behavior and the test we ran to produce that observation (so we can map tests to legal language). If you can include measured error budgets over a 30-day simulated window that would be ideal.

I'll confirm staging access and a contact from infra (ops@heliocare.com) — please include them on the run calendar invite.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — looking forward to the matrix.

— Asha
Asha Patel
Director of Platform Engineering | HelioCare
asha@heliocare.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.inference>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarify SLO parity + next reliability probes (internal)

Looping us for the test plan details — Mina, I'll own the synthetic harness and the SLO comparison table layout. Logan, can you prep a brief note on failover semantics (how we will emulate AZ loss vs our fallback model variants) and the exact metrics we should collect (5xx rate, p50/p95/p99, token-per-second before and after cache warmup)?

Initial plan:
- Ben: create harness (k6 + python driver) and a reproducible config that HelioCare can run.
- Logan: write failover playbook and the tracing hooks we need to collect (span tags for model variant, region, instance id).
- Mina: compile matrix + coordinate calendar invite with Asha/ops.

We should aim to have all artifacts in the Drive folder by EOD Mon. If HelioCare needs us to run the tests in their staging instead of them running, we should be prepared to request limited access (kube exec role) or an SSH jump host.

Ben
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.inference>
To: Asha Patel <asha@heliocare.com>, ops@heliocare.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarify SLO parity + next reliability probes

Thanks both — Asha, appreciate the priorities. We'll deliver the parity matrix and a short 6-step test script that maps directly to your procurement SLA language (we'll annotate which test maps to "availability incident" and how we compute error budgets).

Quick notes on what we'll include in the parity matrix:
- Uptime definition used by each provider (controller-level vs infra-level), including measurement window.
- Rate-limit behavior and burst semantics (headers returned, retry-after semantics, implicit/explicit backoff).
- Failover behavior: detection time, warm routing, model-variant fallback, and expected transient error rates during transition.
- Measured p50/p95/p99 with and without KV cache warmup for 1k and 3k sustained rps profiles.

I'll drop the sheet and harness into the Drive link and create the HubSpot task. Proposed quick sync: Wed 11:00 PT — I will send an invite to you and ops@heliocare.com once Ben and Logan confirm artifact readiness.

Best,
Mina
